intuition: A shorter route can still be slower if it needs unavailable roads. Quantum circuit quality depends on the hardware as well as the gate count.
learningGoal: Explore quantum circuit optimization through gate cancellation, equivalence checks, and hardware-aware cost models.
exerciseNote: CPU-only simulation with Qiskit: compare gate cancellation and ideal operator equivalence. Install the supplied requirements first.

quiz.question: An AI optimization agent produces two implementations of the same quantum computation. Circuit A: 100 gates, 20 qubits. Circuit B: 70 gates, 25 qubits. Both pass the relevant idealized correctness checks. Can we conclude that Circuit B will perform better on real quantum hardware?
quiz.explanation: Ideal equivalence does not establish hardware performance. Depth, routing, gate types, noise, and qubit availability can outweigh a reduction in gate count.
choices: Yes, because fewer gates always means lower error.
Yes, because the qubit count does not matter.
No. We must also examine circuit depth, connectivity, gate types, hardware noise, and the required resource trade-offs.
No, because quantum circuits cannot be optimized.
